substantive_units.result: Exact SAT encoding excludes the entire minimal n=20 opposite-edge core with all A-edges free and five nearby enlarged multisets; X3 and both known star families are positive controls. Scope remains bounded multiplicity.

Arbitrary-multiplicity proof eliminates the opposite-parallel-edge four-star support: physical missing-code matching plus two C10 spoke constraints force C10 A-neighbourhoods inside C10, contradicting diameter to mandatory C11.

Arbitrary-multiplicity proof eliminates the coordinate-face four-star support. Missing-face physical matchings and two C10 spoke constraints leave no common A-neighbour between mandatory complementary C10,C11 classes.

Hostile replay caught omitted C21 in the first opposite-edge proof. Corrected proof forces C21 bridges between C10,C11 and then kills both clean orientations of cube edge 4--6. Coordinate-face proof survives; all 14 affine-plane orbits independently replayed.

Classified the equality case: at n=19 the exactly-four-centre graph is unique up to cube isometry, with five coordinates, one P0, four stars, four coordinate-hub edges and the forced star perfect matching; m=66. All six orientations replay uniquely.

For arbitrary multiplicities in the sole four-centre parity-plane orbit, the induced star graph is necessarily a star forest; hence e(S)<=s-1. This upgrades a construction hypothesis to a structural theorem.
Exact order-20 extremal theorem in four-centre branch: m<=73, with unique equality structure (six coordinate hub plus K1,3 star forest). Exhaustive code-multiset MaxSAT independently agrees.
All edges internal to P0 union P1 satisfy e(P0)+e(P1)+e(P0,P1)<=rq. Same-parity edges inject into distinct missing cross-parity pairs via physical singleton common-neighbour certificates.

Derived joint parity-star missing-pair ledger: with M missing P0-P1 pairs and I same-parity edges, parity-star plus star edges <=s+2(M-I), so the full parity/star block <=rq+M+s-I. Remaining risk is controlling M.

Combined coordinate substitution and parity-star ledger into e(A)<=2C+rq+M+s-I, yielding explicit lower bounds for rooted defect delta and M(n)-m throughout the four-centre branch. Remaining obstruction isolated as joint control of 2C+M.

Closed the full complete-parity subbranch: if P0-P1 is complete (including P1 empty), arbitrary-multiplicity four-centre graphs satisfy m<=M(n). Any surviving counterexample must have a missing physical parity pair.

Closed the whole parity-star-anticomplete subbranch at all orders: coordinate edges <=rt, all parity edges <=rq and nonisolated star forest <=s-1 imply m<=M(n). Any four-centre counterexample must contain a physical parity-star edge.

Constructed and independently verified an actual n=26,m=104 parity-star D2C fixture. It realizes the missing-pair V interface, has deficit 53, and becomes a mandatory positive control. Bounded grid suggests two copies of each star centre are needed but no global minimum claimed.
Every P1 vertex incident to stars has neighbors in all four centre classes; with z active P1 vertices, 4z<=s+M-I. Any P0-star edge forces r>=2 and a second physical copy of its star centre.

Independent rooted/Hall regression of the actual n=26 parity-star fixture: four maximum roots, all p=0, lambda=2, Q=18 or21; no rigid cut. Expands graph coverage while preserving the source-premise trust boundary.

Exact weighted MaxSAT on seven fixed eight-star multisets gives e(A)=rq+14 throughout r=2,3 and q<=4 (q<=3 for r=3). This converts parity-star existence into a sharp missing-pair cancellation conjecture; no general theorem claimed.

Reduced the sharp parity-star bound to the exact deficiency inequality h+L<=s in an obligation-to-missing-pair matching. All seven MaxSAT optima satisfy it sharply; six also refute the tempting stronger claim that every hard obligation can be matched.
